newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Persson says spending plan not one-off deal.
newsitem.headline: Persson says spending plan not one-off deal.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson said on Thursday a proposed 10 billion crown spending package on public services for 1998 would not be a one-off payment.
"The payments will remain over the coming years. It's not a one-off occurrence. It will remain as long as no new tightening is necessary," Persson told reporters.
Persson said on Wednesday he would use a 10 billion crown budget surplus forecast for 1998 on education, health care, care for the elderly and day care.
Persson shrugged off criticism of his plan. Swedish debt yields have risen and the crown has weakened since Persson revealed his plan.
"The bankers are always nervous. In four years we will have a balanced budget...There is room," Persson said.
